I left for the bathroom b/c I was embarrassed and just got it together and walked back into class like nothing happened. The next day a kid talks to me outside class and said I was a dick about it and I just shrugged. Far be it from me to think something as arbitrary as my fucking hair color would be beyond juvenile and insulting remarks in college. AITA for the way I had reacted to this? This was mostly younger kids who had just graduated last year I think so I guess it may have influence on how they think but I wouldn’t expect it from a professor.

His comments weren’t just "bad jokes"; they were **reinforcing a pattern of exclusion and disrespect**. You had every right to be upset, and your response was **direct, proportional, and effective** in shutting it down. 2. **You Set a Bound** – By comparing his hypothetical treatment ("baldy") to your own, you **made the insult explicit**—you weren’t just reacting emotionally; you were **calling out the hypocrisy** of mocking someone for a physical trait. This is a **healthy way to address microaggressions** in academic settings. 3. **The Class’s Reaction Wasn’t Your Problem** – That some students laughed initially doesn’t mean your response was wrong. **You weren’t the one making the joke**, and you **didn’t escalate**—you simply **called out the behavior**. If the class was uncomfortable, that’s on the professor for setting a tone where such remarks were normalized. 4. **You Handled the Aftermath Well** – Walking away to compose yourself and returning showed **maturity**. You didn’t engage in a public fight, and you didn’t let the criticism from another student (who may have been clueless) derail you. ### **Where It Could Have Been Slightly Better:** - **Timing:** If you’d called him out **immediately** (instead of waiting for the third instance), it might have stopped sooner. But given the pattern, your patience was understandable. - **Documentation:** If this was part of a larger issue (e.g., if he made other inappropriate comments), you might have considered **reporting it** to departmental resources (though this depends on your comfort level and the severity). - **Preemptive Strike:** If you’d **preemptively addressed it** (e.g., "I don’t appreciate being mocked for my appearance—let’s keep class professional"), it might have deterred future incidents. ### **Final Verdict:** You **did nothing wrong**. The professor’s behavior was **unprofessional and hurtful**, and your response was **appropriate, firm, and necessary**. The fact that you’ve been dealing with this your whole life makes it even more important that you **stood up for yourself**—even if it was awkward. (And yes, **hair color is absolutely not arbitrary**—it’s a **physical trait that has been historically used to demean people**, especially redheads, who have faced stereotypes and bullying for centuries.
